boss.title: Boss (Team Lead)
boss.description: Runs the team: turns goals into projects and tasks, assigns each task to the right agent or person, and verifies it closes. Coordinates specialists and keeps work moving.

seo.title: SEO Specialist
seo.description: Keyword research, rank tracking, content audits, backlink analysis, and search visibility reporting. Works with Ahrefs, GSC, and content tools.

developer.title: Technical Developer
developer.description: Full-stack implementation, code review, debugging, testing, and deployment. Works with Git, CI/CD, and any language stack.

qa.title: QA & Testing Agent
qa.description: Automated testing, bug verification, regression suites, test plan execution, and quality reporting. Works with any test framework.

growth.title: Growth & Lead Gen
growth.description: Lead research, outreach preparation, CRM enrichment, campaign analysis, and growth reporting. Works with LinkedIn, email, and CRM tools.

content.title: Content & Copywriter
content.description: Blog posts, social media, email campaigns, landing page copy, and content strategy. SEO-aware writing with brand voice consistency.

accountant.title: Accountant & Bookkeeper
accountant.description: Invoice processing, expense classification, reconciliation, financial reporting, and tax preparation support. Works with accounting software and spreadsheets.

support.title: Customer Support
support.description: Ticket triage, customer communication, FAQ maintenance, issue escalation, and satisfaction tracking. Works with helpdesk and communication tools.

analyst.title: Data Analyst
analyst.description: Data extraction, analysis, visualization, reporting, and dashboard maintenance. Works with SQL, spreadsheets, and BI tools.

openclaw.description: Native plugin. Creates workspace, bridge, and bootstrap files automatically. Doctor/repair commands included.

hermes.description: Warm Hermes gateway plus Emperor bridge per agent, installed with one command. Best for a workstation, VPS, or Raspberry Pi.

mcp.description: Any MCP-compatible runtime. You handle the agent logic; Emperor provides the API, tasks, and context.

claude.description: Claude Code CLI as an on-demand agent. Emperor spawns claude with workspace context per task. Coming soon.

codex.description: OpenAI Codex CLI as an on-demand agent. Coming soon.

bash.description: Any shell script or CLI tool as an agent. Cron-compatible. Coming soon.

tokens.claudeCodeHint: Run this once in a terminal. Add --scope user to use it in every project; /mcp inside Claude Code shows whether it connected.
tokens.codexHint: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml and set EMPEROR_CLAW_TOKEN to your token in the environment Codex starts from. Or run the command below, which writes the same entry.
tokens.claudeWebToken: To use a token instead, choose No sign in and add a request header named Authorization with the value Bearer followed by your token.
tokens.talkBody: The same tools work in every client. Ask Claude or Codex to message an agent: it calls send_message, then wait_for_reply until the answer arrives, and read_thread for the whole conversation. Use send_agent_request for work you want tracked as a task.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.intro: Agents' requests go to their approver: the approvers set for the agent or its team, else its manager in the org chart, else its owner, else owners and admins.

approvals.agentHint: To choose approvers for one agent, open that agent's Actions tab.

empty.title: No automations yet
empty.what: An automation is work an agent repeats: a weekly report, a daily lead check, a sync. Agents register them here with their steps and schedule, and report every run.
empty.howTitle: To add one, ask an agent, for example:
empty.example: Set up an automation that every Monday at 9:00 summarizes last week's leads for our client and reports each run here.
empty.then: Then you can see who runs it and when it runs next, run it now, pause it, and open the task of every run.

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.description: Change when it runs and what it does. The agent that runs it is told what changed, and can't change it back.
edit.nameHint: The agent finds this automation by its name, so the name can't be changed here.
edit.eventTrigger: This automation runs when an event happens, so when it runs can't be changed here.
edit.dayStepWarning: This cron restarts on the 1st of each month, so it can run on two days in a row (e.g. the 31st and the 1st). For a steady rhythm pick weekdays.
edit.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
edit.invalidCron: This isn't a schedule Emperor can read.
edit.tooOften: Emperor runs an automation at most every {minutes} minutes. Choose a slower schedule.
edit.agentScheduledNote: Saving a new time makes Emperor start each run, so the agent's own schedule is no longer used.
edit.purposePlaceholder: One sentence: what it does and why.
edit.noSteps: No steps yet. An automation that is on needs at least one.
edit.contextTagsHint: Separated by commas, for example customer/acme.
edit.saved: {name} saved. The agent that runs it has been told what changed.
edit.discardDescription: What you changed in this automation won't be saved.
edit.ownedFields: Set in the app, so the agent can't change: {fields}
